input: Research acoustic panel options for the home studio

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Acoustic treatment needs differ significantly between absorption, diffusion, and bass trapping — knowing which problems to solve narrows the research dramatically.
Room size, shape, and current surfaces determine how many panels are needed and what placement strategy makes sense.
Whether this is for recording vocals, mixing, podcasting, or music production changes which acoustic properties matter most.
Budget range determines whether to research DIY builds, mid-range retail panels, or professional-grade solutions.
Whether the user wants to buy ready-made panels or build their own is a fork in the road that leads to completely different research paths.
Some users prioritise aesthetics and want panels to blend into decor; others only care about acoustic performance — this shapes which products to highlight.
Knowing what a good outcome looks like — a shortlist, a buying decision, a comparison document — defines how deep the research needs to go.

gold.taskTitle: Research acoustic panels for home studio
gold.taskDescription: Find and evaluate acoustic panel options suitable for a home studio setup.

questions.title: What is the primary use of your home studio?
questions.description: Identify whether the studio is used for vocal recording, music production, mixing, podcasting, etc. This determines which acoustic properties (e.g. reflection control vs. low-end treatment) matter most.

questions.title: Which acoustic problem are you mainly trying to fix?
questions.description: Determine whether the focus is on reducing echo/reflections, controlling bass buildup, diffusing sound, or a full treatment — this scopes the type of panels to research.

questions.title: What are the dimensions of the room being treated?
questions.description: Room size and shape directly affect how many panels are needed and what thickness or NRC rating to target.

questions.title: What is your total budget for this project?
questions.description: A clear budget range (e.g. under $200, $200–$600, $600+) determines whether to focus on DIY options, consumer brands, or pro-grade products.

questions.title: Do you prefer buying ready-made panels or building your own?
questions.description: This is a key fork — DIY research involves materials, frames, and fabric sourcing, while ready-made research focuses on brands and retailers.

questions.title: How important is the visual appearance of the panels to you?
questions.description: Understanding whether aesthetics are a priority (colour, fabric, shape) vs. purely functional helps filter which products or DIY designs to highlight.

questions.title: What should the research result in — a shortlist, a single recommendation, or a comparison?
questions.description: Defines the output format and depth of research needed to consider the task complete.
